qa.a: I don't. I try and skip them as soon as they come on. Unless it's a trailer for a game or a book or a movie I'd like to see. Or an ad on this podcast. Those are usually quite entertaining, aren't they?

qa.q: Do you watch them from the beginning to the end?
qa.a: Only if they're interesting or if I can't reach the skip option in time. I sometimes have, um, YouTube on while I work out, and it's difficult to do crunches and reach over at the same time, so I just have to put up with them until they're done, or I am.

qa.q: How do you feel about advertisements?
qa.a: Uh, usually I think ads are just a way of getting people to dislike your product before they even look at it. Um, however, some ads are quite brilliant and funny, like the Iron Brew adverts, for example. They usually have a, a story or a joke, and there's one for Solaris which has great music to match the visuals.

qa.q: What advertising do you have in your country?
qa.a: Oh, it's everywhere. We have billboards and posters and viral marketing and YouTube ads inserted into videos and ads in the breaks of TV shows. I, I think the only respite is on the BBC, and even they have them for their programs.

qa.q: Is there much advertising in your country?
qa.a: I think it's everywhere, isn't it? And it's rather sophisticated at that. Um, especially online where your, your cookies are used to track what you look at, and, um, they send you almost tailor-made adverts, don't they?

It's probably easier to say where you can't see advertising, frankly speaking. It's all over social media and, uh, well, any online media, newspapers, TV. Some people even get paid to be branded with tattoos or wear goods with advertising slogans. That's a bit depressing.

qa.q: What do you think is the purpose of advertising?
qa.a: In a nutshell, uh, to make money. It's all about getting attention and getting customers to buy your good or service. Um, there are some adverts for social services, and, uh, PSAs like that aren't usually classed as adverts, and they're very few and far between.

qa.q: Have you ever bought anything because of adverts?
qa.a: Not directly. It's usually been word of mouth, to be honest. Um, so maybe that's indirect advertising of a kind, but nothing like what we discussed already.
